newsitem.title: GERMANY: Villeroy & Boch says plans to omit 1996 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Villeroy & Boch says plans to omit 1996 dividend.

text.p: German bathroom fittings and tableware maker Villeroy & Boch said on Friday it planned to omit its dividend for 1996, warning that major restructuring costs had pushed it into loss last year.

Villeroy, which has been on a downward spiral in recent years, hurt by higher production costs in the domestic market and the economic recession which hit in the early 1990s, said group sales fell by two percent in 1996 to 1.453 billion marks.

"The shortfall in sales, which had been 9.7 percent at the end of the first quarter of 1996, clearly narrowed over the year, although the development in the three main business units was mixed," the company said in a statement.
It went on: "Because of new and existing measures aimed at improving earnings and strengthening the group strategically, a loss in the 1996 business year looks unavoidable."

Villeroy said it would be proposing to the supervisory board that no dividend be paid on 1996 earnings. The previous year the group had paid out a dividend of 7.50 marks per preference share and 6.30 marks per ordinary share.

Sales at Villeroy & Boch's tiles unit and tableware unit grew 3.1 percent and 2.2 percent respectively during the year, while sales at its bathroom fittings unit fell 11.2 percent because of recession in the construction industry.

The foreign share of Villeroy's business increased to 46.1 percent in 1996 from 43.7 percent a year earlier and the group said it had compensated for a large chunk of domestic losses through higher exports.
